articles.title: Democrats Win House, Poised to Take Senate
articles.summary: In an outcome seen as a backlash to President Donald Trump, Democrats were projected as easily capturing a majority of seats in the House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. Control of the Senate was still too close to call heading into the evening hours Tuesday.
body: “This is the repudiation of Trumpism that people have been hoping for,” CNN political commentator Van Jones said about the expected “Blue Wave.”

The surge of support for Democrats comes as Trump’s approval ratings among American voters has plummeted over the course of the year, amid higher gas and grocery prices and the administration’s unpopular war with Iran. As of Nov. 3, just 37% of U.S. voters approve of Trump, near his lowest level ever of 36% just two weeks ago, per the New York Times’ analysis of multiple polls. Trump has stumped for Republican candidates at rallies across the country in recent weeks.

Among the 35 Senate races in contention in 2026, Democrats were ahead in several closely watched races Tuesday night, according to the AP results. Those included James Talarico vs. Ken Paxton in Texas; Dr. Abdul El-Sayed vs. Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan; and Troy Jackson vs. Republican incumbent Susan Collins in Maine. Roy Cooper decisively beat Michael Whatley in the Senate race in North Carolina, and Annie Andrews was the projected winner in South Carolina over Darline Graham.

articles.title: Weta FX and TAICCA Partner to Turn Taiwan Into an AI Screen Production Hub for Asia (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Weta FX, the New Zealand visual effects house behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “Avatar,” is teaming with the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) on a plan to turn Taiwan into a center for AI-driven screen production in Asia. The partnership will be formally launched on Nov.
body: TAICCA chair Sue Wang will appear at the event alongside three Weta FX executives: CEO Daniel Seah, chief technology officer Kimball Thurston and VFX supervisor Sheldon Stopsack.

The pact pairs Taiwan’s AI and advanced-tech capabilities and its pool of creative talent with what Weta FX brings to the table – VFX know-how, a track record on international productions and a global network. The aim is to plug Taiwanese technologists and creatives into work across the worldwide screen business.
For Seah, the deal carries a personal angle. He grew up in Taiwan. The studio has also been building ties on the island, appearing at the Taoyuan International Film & Technology Forum in August.

The tie-up fits within TAICCA’s wider brief, which takes in the use of new technologies to make content. TTXC Innovations, a recently concluded market platform, is one case in point. It was built to help bring cultural content and tech to market by putting creators, tech developers, investors, buyers and distributors in the same room.

articles.title: Lucy Liu’s ‘The Pirate Queen’ Expands With Graphic Novel, New Game and International Tour as Creator Eloise Singer Joins BAFTA Breakthrough Cohort (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Lucy Liu and Eloise Singer are preparing to take “The Pirate Queen: No Safe Waters,” their immersive experience about Chinese pirate leader Cheng Shih, on an international tour next year, Singer tells Variety. The pair have also co-written a graphic novel and are developing a new game.
body: The franchise is built around a retelling of the stories about real life character Cheng Shih, who was a powerful female pirate in the South China Sea at the beginning of the 18th century.

“No Safe Waters” played in the Cannes Film Festival’s Immersive Competition this year, with Liu narrating and producing alongside Singer. It follows the original 2024 VR version of “The Pirate Queen,” which earned an Emmy nomination.

Liu says Cheng Shih was intelligent and strategically brilliant, and won respect through negotiation and leadership “in a world designed to exclude women entirely.” In Liu’s view, the pirate leader defies nearly every stereotype historically placed on Asian women in storytelling. “She was politically astute, ruthless when necessary, deeply strategic, and completely self-determined. Stories like hers remind us that history has always contained powerful, complex women – they were never centered in mainstream narratives,” Liu tells Variety. “That’s beginning to change, and I think audiences are hungry for stories that feel more expansive.”

articles.title: Park Hoon-jung’s Assassin Noir ‘Tristes Tropiques’ Sells to North America, France, Spain
articles.summary: “Tristes Tropiques,” the latest genre outing from “New World” and “The Witch” director Park Hoon-jung, has been picked up for North America by Well Go USA as Finecut, which is carrying the film in its AFM line-up, closes a fresh round of deals ahead of the film’s Nov.
body: The new pacts build on sales unveiled earlier to Splendid Film for Germany, Austria and Switzerland; Media4Fun for Poland; Multivision India for the Indian subcontinent; PT Prima Cinema Multimedia for Indonesia; and Izagur Media for Mongolia.

The story centers on a band of young killers trained by Master, who holds absolute sway over a tropical rainforest. Then Master turns up dead. Nobody knows who killed him, and the assassins begin to distrust one another.

The cast features Lee Sin-young (“Rebound”), Park Yu-rim (“Drive My Car”), Kim Myung-min (“Your Honor”) and Park Hae-soo (“Squid Game”). Taiwanese actors Austin Lin (“96 Minutes”), Chen Yi-Wen (“The Pig, the Snake and the Pigeon”) and Wang Po-Chieh (“Eye of the Storm”) are also part of the ensemble.

Well Go USA has a track record with the filmmaker, having released “The Witch” films and “The Childe” in North America. Doris Pfardrescher, the company’s president and CEO, said: “We’re thrilled to continue our relationship with Park Hoon-jung. ‘Tristes Tropiques’ takes his signature blend of style, emotion, and hard-hitting action to a whole new level.”

articles.title: Peter Medak obituary
articles.summary: Film and television director who won plaudits for The Ruling Class, The Changeling and The Krays. In 2013, when Martin Scorsese compiled a brief list of his favourite horror films, he placed the eerie and overlooked 1980 ghost story The Changeling in the company of classics such as The Shining, The…
body: The Changeling concerns a composer ( George C Scott ) who is grieving the deaths of his wife and daughter in a road accident. After moving into a long-vacant Seattle mansion where things start going bump in the night, he becomes convinced that a spectral presence is trying to communicate with him.

A generation raised on slasher films might now be underwhelmed by the low-key frights, which include a bath that runs itself, a cobwebbed wheelchair and visions of a child’s face warped underwater. But with its subtlety and patience, and the prioritising of atmosphere over revelation, the movie remains chilling today.

It represented a rare foray into horror for Medak, who was already admired for The Ruling Class (1972), a madcap satire starring an Oscar-nominated Peter O’Toole as an aristocrat who believes himself to be Jesus Christ. The critic Janet Maslin identified in the director a “droll affinity for eccentric behaviour”.

articles.title: Why Kim Kardashian came back to 'the worst TV drama ever'
articles.summary: The media personality and businesswoman says she's worked on her acting for series two of All's Fair.
body: It was meant to be Kim Kardashian's triumphant debut as a leading actor - but last year's legal drama All's Fair was so universally panned by critics that it actually broke streaming records as audiences clambered to see what all the fuss was about.
Kardashian, who is best known as a media personality and businesswoman, tells the BBC she had no choice but to "lean into" the discourse and come back for a second series.
"We thought we were this law show, dealing with some really serious issues," she jokes.
But viewers mostly enjoyed its comedy value - with outlandish outfits and zingy one-liners from co-stars Sarah Paulson and Glenn Close sending the show straight into the pantheon of 'camp classics'.

articles.title: China’s first AI-generated film is a flop. Some still see it as the future of cinema
articles.summary: Chinese investors placing high value on AI despite unpopularity of Sanxingdui: Future Past. China’s first fully AI-generated movie has flopped, earning just 1.7m yuan (£191,000) at the box office despite costing “tens of millions” to make, according to its producer. But is it any good?
body: But is it any good? The Guardian watched Sanxingdui: Future Past in a virtually empty cinema in Beijing, and found it no worse than plenty of human-centred mindless action flicks.

Sanxingdui tells a confusing tale of a future society in which every decision has been outsourced to algorithms and AI, leading to a global catastrophe. The only way to avert the impending doom is to unlock the hidden code that is hidden in the Sanxingdui, bronze sculptures linked to the ancient kingdom of Shu. Cue astronauts racing through ancient Egypt and archeologists diving through space-time vortices.
All of the film’s visuals and some of its sound effects were created using AI, while it was edited by humans.

articles.title: Mum, I’m Alien Pregnant review – slime and silliness in amusing New Zealand comedy horror
articles.summary: Mucus, alien gristle, a tentacle-bearing penis and, of course, the pregnancy of the title are all borne with deadpan calmness in this underplayed comedy. In this amusingly silly exercise in gross-out body horror and bathos from New Zealand, thirtysomething underachiever Mary (Hannah Lynch) finds…
body: Fortunately, the cast is well up for serving this sort of underplayed comedy, especially supporting players Yvette Parsons and Jackie van Beek, as Mary and Arlo’s single mums Cynthia and Ann respectively. For example, somewhere towards the end (and don’t worry, there’s nothing to spoil here), Cynthia gets a little het up about Mary farting too much, after a nest of mucus, tissue and alien gristle shoots out of Mary’s nether regions. Ann, on the other hand, gets quite concerned about the mess all this is making of her immaculate flat, and keeps apologising for the disorder to anyone who shows up, including unflappable paramedics Sofia (Karen O’Leary) and Sophie (Ariadne Baltazar).

Is it all meant to be a parable about the anxieties of single motherhood and the changes pregnancy wreaks on the female body? Yes, sure, if you want. But subtext is less the point than slow burns and slime, and that honest directness make the end result rather winning.

articles.title: Chris Pappas Becomes First Openly Gay Man Elected to Senate
articles.summary: Elsewhere in history-making results from the 2026 midterms, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor, with her win in Georgia.
body: Chris Pappas is set to become the first openly gay male U.S. senator, following his projected defeat of former U.S. Sen. John E. Sununu in New Hampshire.
The Democrat is the third LGBTQ+ person to be elected to the Senate, following former senators Tammy Baldwin and Kyrsten Sinema.
His victory keeps the open Senate seat in Democratic control as Pappas and Sununu were facing off against retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen.

“Tonight’s results are a wake-up call for corporate special interests and billionaires who have been rigging the economy, for the cowards in Congress who have enabled health care cuts, tariffs and war and for the incompetent president who can’t even be bothered to care how people are being hurt,” he added.

articles.title: Andrew Scott drama Elsinore leads British independent film award nominations
articles.summary: Elsinore is in contention for 12 Bifas, including for Scott’s highly praised performance, while Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, Ashley Walters’ Animol and Mike Leigh’s Tender Loving Care are also recognised.
body: Elsinore, the drama in which Andrew Scott plays the actor Ian Charleson as he takes on Shakespeare’s Hamlet in the last months of his life, before he died of Aids in 1990, has emerged as the leading contender for the British independent film awards (Bifas).

The film, which is directed by Simon Stone and co-stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper and Johnny Flynn, received 12 nominations, including best British independent film, best director for Stone and best lead performance for Scott. Elsinore has collected rave reviews since its premiere at the Telluride film festival in September, with the Guardian’s Benjamin Lee describing it as “a devastating movie [that] is a reminder of Charleson’s strength and the many men like him and it implores us to remember them too”. Scott is also already being tipped as the favourite for the best actor Oscar – and he would be the first out gay actor to win.

articles.title: ‘The Incomer’ Attracted Domhnall Gleeson and Moby and Got Its Creator on the BAFTA Breakthrough List. Now, He’s Working on a Plan B Film.
articles.summary: Scottish writer-director Louis Paxton takes THR through his feature debut, how much it reflects real-life experiences and what’s next for him.
body: Scottish writer-director Louis Paxton ’s debut feature film, the dark comedy-drama The Incomer, has star power – in the form of Domhnall Gleeson ( Star Wars sequel trilogy), Gayle Rankin ( House of the Dragon ), John Hannah ( The Mummy franchise) and others. It also has an oddball, quirky vibe. And it has the backing of Focus Features, Universal Pictures International and Moby.

The Incomer is set on a remote Scottish island and follows siblings who have lived in peaceful isolation for decades, hunting seabirds, chatting to mythic creatures, and defending their isle from dreaded Incomers. Their world is upended with the arrival of Daniel (Gleeson), an awkward council worker, tasked with moving them to the mainland.
Paxton talked to THR about the star-studded offbeat movie, how Moby got involved, his hopes for the BAFTA Breakthrough experience and what else is next for him.
